issues.legal_issue: Railway property acquired after the applicable constitutional tax-exemption cutoff is not liable to municipal tax under an earlier notification unless a later law or notification makes it liable.
material_facts: The railway administration constructed the assessed buildings after 1 April 1937; some were also constructed after the Constitution commenced.
A 1911 notification under the Indian Railways Act, 1890, had declared the railway administration liable for specified municipal taxes, including taxes in the municipality concerned.
No notification under section 3 of the Railways (Local Authorities Taxation) Act, 1941, declared the railway property liable for the taxes, and no other applicable law provided for its taxation.
The municipality assessed the buildings and sought to collect municipal tax; the railway administration challenged that liability.
issues.conclusion: The buildings were exempt from municipal tax, and the municipality could not levy or collect the tax on them. The earlier notification did not make later-acquired railway property liable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 154 of the Government of India Act, 1935, exempted Union property from provincial and local taxes, subject to the proviso preserving liability only for property that was already liable immediately before Part III commenced. Article 285 of the Constitution similarly exempts Union property, with clause (2) preserving only pre-existing tax liability. Section 4 of the Railways (Local Authorities Taxation) Act, 1941, permits revocation or variation of notifications issued under section 135 of the Indian Railways Act, 1890; it does not itself impose tax liability on later-acquired property. Section 3 of the 1941 Act requires a notification declaring railway property liable. The Court applied Corporation of Calcutta v. Governors of St. Thomas’ School, Calcutta, which held that government-built structures not taxable before the 1935 Act commenced were not brought within the grandfathering proviso.

predicates.railway_municipal_tax_appeal: The proceeding challenges a municipality’s levy or collection of tax on property held for railway administration purposes.
predicates.property_acquired_after_exemption_cutoff: The property was not in existence and was not liable to the relevant local tax when the applicable constitutional exemption took effect.
predicates.no_later_tax_authorization: No later law or notification made the property liable to the local tax.

issues.definition: When a railway municipal-tax appeal concerns property acquired after the applicable exemption cutoff and no later tax authorization applies, the property is exempt from municipal tax.
